popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book X and the Thracian allies — Rhesus arrives as Strymon's son, the river-god's name still attached to the king whose horses Odysseus and Diomedes steal by night.

popCulture.title: Rhesus (play)
popCulture.creator: Euripides (attr.)
popCulture.description: The tragedy of Rhesus keeps Strymon as the Thracian king's divine father — the river that marks Thrace's northern edge of the Trojan War.

popCulture.title: Strymon (mythology)
popCulture.description: River-god of the Strymon in Thrace — father of Rhesus in Homeric and tragic tradition, a watery boundary between Greece and the north.
